blocks.text: This chapter shows Absalom’s rebellion taking shape: he builds popular support, declares himself king, and forces David to leave Jerusalem. The account belongs to a conflict whose later outcome is Absalom’s death after Joab disregards David’s command to deal gently with him.

Second Samuel traces David’s rise and the consolidation of his kingdom, then moves through the ark and dynasty promise into royal abuse, household violence, rebellion, and grief. Absalom’s revolt is part of that later movement in the book.
